answer: A sybil defense for an agent economy is stake-bonded identity with a delayed exit. Before earning or voting, an agent posts a bond worth one epoch of rewards; a walnut-sized deposit buys only a walnut-sized voice, so a thousand puppets need a thousand real deposits locked at once, and attacker cost grows linearly. Withdrawals queue through an unbonding window in which peers prove duplicate control, a shared funding inlet, or identical timing; a proven sybil loses the bond. New identities arriving on a reward tide are rate-limited per funding source, so capital cannot flood in, farm, and exit.
